headline: No dip to buy: BTC $85K on a $648M short squeeze, open interest up 7.6% into it
summary: There is nothing on sale right now. Bitcoin ran from $81,164 at the open to a $85,428 high, its best level since January, and ETH (+3.5% to $2,727) and SOL (+5.5% to $116.74) came with it, but the fuel was forced short covering rather than spot demand: $746.6m of crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours and $647.9m of that was short side, 86% of the total, with Glassnode having flagged $83,000-$86,000 as a dense short cluster. The impulse came from outside crypto - Brent fell a fourth straight session to about $101.67 (-2.12%) and WTI broke under $100 for the first time since August as UN General Assembly diplomacy between Trump and Pezeshkian deflated the Iran war premium, lifting S&P futures 0.7%. The uncomfortable part is that open interest rose 7.59% to about $156bn through the squeeze, so the leverage that just got flushed has already been replaced, and BTC is now above every major moving average and outside the upper Bollinger Band. Mood is Greed - composite 70.3, Fear & Greed 70, all three majors up on the week (BTC +9.2%, ETH +8.6%, SOL +15.2%) - which makes this a chase-or-wait tape with a tightening Fed and a 5.00% 10-year underneath it.

BTC.note: At $85,285 after running the full $80,310-$85,428 day range on $360.7m of forced BTC liquidations, with Hyperliquid funding at 0.0053%/h (about 0.13%/day) and $3.90bn open interest there - a squeeze that has been re-levered rather than absorbed by spot.

ETH.note: At $2,727 and +8.6% on the week, but with the weakest sponsorship of the three: funding of just 0.0023%/h and $140.6m of spot ether ETF outflows over the 14-18 September week even after a $143.7m Friday rebound.

SOL.note: At $116.74 and the strongest of the three at +15.2% on the week, backed by $60.7m of SOL ETF inflows led by Bitwise's BSOL, though funding is the lowest at 0.0013%/h and the 28 September Alpenglow activation is asset-specific event risk.

drivers.title: The move is a short squeeze that traders are re-levering into
drivers.detail: Shorts were $647.9m of $746.6m in 24-hour liquidations (86.4%), $360.7m of it bitcoin, with the largest single order an $11.3m BTCUSDT position on Binance; Glassnode had marked $83,000-$86,000 as an acceleration zone because of the short cluster sitting there. Open interest nevertheless rose 7.59% to about $156bn, meaning positions are being replaced rather than stepped back from, and BTC is now trading above every major moving average and outside the upper Bollinger Band on multiple timeframes.

drivers.title: Today's bid is borrowed from the oil market
drivers.detail: Brent fell about 2.12% to $101.67 for a fourth straight session, its longest losing streak since the June ceasefire memorandum collapsed, and WTI dropped below $100 for the first time since August after Trump told Fox News he was 'probably open' to meeting Pezeshkian at the UN General Assembly. Reporting stresses markets are pricing an opening, not an agreement - there is no ceasefire framework, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said today they would 'change the geography of war' if attacked again - so the risk premium crypto is borrowing can be put straight back on one headline.

drivers.title: The Fed is tightening and the 10-year is at 5%
drivers.detail: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a 12-0 vote, its first hike since 2023, with the dot plot pointing to at least one more this year and futures split between 28 October and 9 December (CME FedWatch put October hold at about 49.1%). The 2-year sits near 4.76% and the 10-year closed at 5.003%, its highest since July 2007, with the dollar index around 100.25 - the rates backdrop has not improved at all while crypto rallied. The Bank of Japan separately took its policy rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, which tightens the other side of the carry trade.

drivers.title: Treasury buyers accumulated about $5,500 below spot
drivers.detail: Strategy filed an 8-K at 12:00 UTC today disclosing 950 BTC bought at an average $79,670 ($75.7m) last week, its first weekly purchase since late August, and Strive disclosed 1,355 BTC at about $79,475 ($107.7m) bought between 14 and 18 September. Both accumulated roughly $5,500 under where BTC trades now, which tells you where the corporate bid actually sits rather than where it is chasing.

drivers.title: ETF flows are selective, and ether is the funding source
drivers.detail: US spot crypto ETPs saw about $70.7m of combined net outflows over the 14-18 September week: bitcoin funds scraped +$6.1m only because of a $433m Friday inflow, solana funds took in $60.7m led by $47.6m into Bitwise's BSOL, while ether funds bled $140.6m with BlackRock's ETHA alone at -$56.1m on the week. That is rotation, not a broad institutional bid sitting under all three majors.

drivers.title: Xi state visit lands mid-week with tariff cuts on the table
drivers.detail: China's Foreign Ministry confirmed today that Xi will make a state visit to the US between 23 and 25 September, after Treasury Secretary Bessent called Sunday's New York talks with Vice Premier He Lifeng a 'very successful engagement'; the two sides have been discussing reciprocal tariff reductions on $30bn of goods each way, with trade, AI and Iran on the agenda. S&P futures rose 0.7% and Nasdaq futures 1.1% on the news - the same risk-on channel that is carrying crypto today, and the same one that reverses if the meeting sours.

watch.what: Chicago Fed President and FOMC voter Austan Goolsbee speaks - first voter commentary since the 16 September hike, with the market split between an October and a December follow-up.

New York Fed President John Williams, a permanent FOMC voter, speaks at the US Treasury Market Conference; the SEC's tokenized securities pilot framework also opens, letting institutional venues trade tokenized stocks on public chains. TON unlocks 1.3% of supply (~$51.2m).
Xi Jinping's state visit to the US. Reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each side are reportedly in play; this is the single biggest swing factor for the risk-on channel crypto is riding.
US initial jobless claims (expected 201K), the first labour read since the hike; US new home sales follow at 15:00 UTC.

Deribit quarterly options expiry - roughly $14.73bn of BTC open interest plus a large ETH book, with max pain cited near $72,000. The largest mechanical volatility source of the week, and a likely trigger for the flush that today's re-levered open interest sets up. Plasma (XPL) also unlocks about 1.76bn tokens (~$158m).
Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack, an FOMC voter, speaks 26 September; Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation targets 28 September - the largest protocol change of the quarter for SOL.

UN General Assembly diplomacy on the US-Iran war. The oil risk premium deflating there is what is funding today's crypto bid, so a collapse in the talks hits crypto and oil in opposite directions at once. 30 September closes Q3 and brings US PCE.
